C++ RuntimeService Getting Started

This page covers the four common RuntimeService workflows. See the full C++ RuntimeService reference for all options.

0. Create a client

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include "atom_sdk/core/json.hpp"
#include <iostream>
#include <filesystem>

namespace json = atom::sdk::json;
atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
auto& runtime = client.runtime();
const std::string graph_name = "detection_graph";

1. List graphs

auto graphs = runtime.list_graphs();
for (const auto& graph : graphs) {
    std::cout << json::serialize(graph) << "\n";
}

Print the JSON once to confirm the graph-name field returned by your service.

2. Run a graph and read its result

2.1 Normal mode

Normal mode uses one or more RuntimeFrame objects. The frame can be built from a file, complete EPICRAW bytes, or raw image and point-cloud data.

json::value roi = json::parse(R"({
  "min": {"x": -0.5, "y": -0.5, "z": 0.1},
  "max": {"x": 0.5, "y": 0.5, "z": 2.0},
  "cam2ROIFrame": [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
})");
runtime.load_graph(graph_name);
auto frame = atom::sdk::RuntimeFrame::from_file(
    "/data/frame.epicraw",
    json::parse("[0,0,0,0,0,0]"),
    roi);
auto result = runtime.run_graph({graph_name, {frame}});
std::cout << json::serialize(result) << "\n";

For camera or network data, use RuntimeFrame::from_bytes(…​) and pass the bytes directly. For raw image and point-cloud data, use RuntimeFrame::from_data(…​).

If your application has raw image and point-cloud data, build the frame in memory with RuntimeFrame::from_data(…​):

auto points = get_point_values_from_camera();
auto image_bytes = get_image_bytes_from_camera();
atom::sdk::RuntimePointData point_data{points, 640, 480, 3};
atom::sdk::RuntimeImageData image_data{image_bytes, 640, 480, 3, 1};
auto frame_from_data = atom::sdk::RuntimeFrame::from_data(
    point_data, image_data,
    json::parse("[0,0,0,0,0,0]"),
    json::parse("[[600,0,320],[0,600,240],[0,0,1]]"),
    json::parse("[0,0,0,0,0]"));
frame_from_data.roi = roi;
auto result = runtime.run_graph({graph_name, {frame_from_data}});

Replace the two capture functions with your camera or acquisition code.

2.2 Passive-binocular mode

Use RuntimeRunParams::passive_bino_from_file/bytes/images(…​) when the graph input is configured as passive_bino.

auto params = atom::sdk::RuntimeRunParams::passive_bino_from_bytes(
    graph_name,
    get_epicraw3_bytes_from_camera(),
    json::parse("[0,0,0,0,0,0]"));
auto result = runtime.run_graph(params);

For three raw images, use passive_bino_from_images(…​) and provide the three camera metadata objects.

If your application has three raw passive-binocular images, use passive_bino_from_images(…​):

json::object camera_params;
camera_params["CameraMatrix"] = json::array{600, 0, 320, 0, 600, 240, 0, 0, 1};
camera_params["CameraDistortion"] = json::array{0, 0, 0, 0, 0};
camera_params["CameraRotation"] = json::array{1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1};
camera_params["CameraTranslation"] = json::array{0, 0, 0};
json::object passive_params;
passive_params["DepthSrc1"] = camera_params;
passive_params["DepthSrc2"] = camera_params;
passive_params["TextureSrc"] = camera_params;
auto params = atom::sdk::RuntimeRunParams::passive_bino_from_images(
    graph_name,
    {atom::sdk::RuntimePassiveBinoImage{depth_src1, 640, 480, 2},
     atom::sdk::RuntimePassiveBinoImage{depth_src2, 640, 480, 2},
     atom::sdk::RuntimePassiveBinoImage{texture_bgr, 640, 480, 16}},
    passive_params,
    json::parse("[0,0,0,0,0,0]"));
auto result = runtime.run_graph(params);

The image order is fixed: DepthSrc1, DepthSrc2, TextureSrc. 2 is CV_16UC1; 16 is CV_8UC3.

2.3 Read output bindings

auto info = runtime.get_binded_outputs_info(graph_name);
std::cout << json::serialize(info) << "\n";

auto value = runtime.get_binded_output_value(
    {graph_name, "detection_result"});
std::cout << json::serialize(value) << "\n";

auto clouds = runtime.get_binded_point_cloud_parsed(
    {graph_name, "filtered_cloud", 3});

To read a node result, configure that node port as an output binding first. RuntimeService cannot query an arbitrary node port by node_id.

runtime.release_graph(graph_name);

3. Run one algorithm without a graph

atom::sdk::SingleNodeParams params;
params.node_name = "EstimateNormal";
params.inputs["points"] = std::filesystem::path("/data/scan.ply");

auto parsed = runtime.run_single_node_no_graph_parsed(params);
auto raw = runtime.run_single_node_no_graph(params);

The parsed result exposes JSON, point-cloud, or image values by output-port name. The raw method keeps the service response unchanged.

4. Change parameters and run again

runtime.load_graph(graph_name);
auto meta = runtime.get_meta_info(graph_name);
std::cout << json::serialize(meta) << "\n";

atom::sdk::JsonObject shared;
shared["camera_id"] = "cam-01";
runtime.set_shared_params({graph_name, shared});

atom::sdk::JsonObject run_params;
run_params["confidence"] = 0.8;
runtime.set_run_params({graph_name, run_params});

auto result = runtime.run_graph({graph_name, {frame}});
auto value = runtime.get_binded_output_value(
    {graph_name, "detection_result"});

Replace the example parameter and binding names with the names returned by the service.
